concepts_addressed: VSL as Qualification and Pre-Frame Gate
Cross-Platform Retargeting Increases Touchpoints and Reduces CAC
Platform Choice and Backup Channel Resilience
Show-Up Rate and Lead Nurture Optimization

frameworks.name: 70-20-10 Ad Budget Allocation
frameworks.definition: Allocate 70% of ad resources to proven winners, 20% to adjacent permutations of those winners, and 10% to wild experimental ideas; mirrors how time is spent daily on creative production.

frameworks.name: Proof Continuum
frameworks.definition: A spectrum of proof credibility for ads: anonymous text testimonials at the low end; in-person, live, look-alike, specific-result demonstrations at the high end. Each dimension (in-person vs virtual, live vs recorded, similar avatar vs dissimilar, specific desired result vs generic) increases or decreases believability.

frameworks.name: Four Group Funnel Conversion Mechanisms
frameworks.definition: Four ways to convert free-group members into paid clients: (1) free onboarding call for every new member that pivots to a sales conversation; (2) five-video series inside the group acting as a broken-up VSL covering opportunity, core story, three belief-breaking stories, and CTA; (3) weekly webinar with soft CTA where setters pull engaged chatters; (4) DM setters engaging anyone who likes, comments, or posts.
frameworks.concept: Show-Up Rate and Lead Nurture Optimization

frameworks.name: Friction Calibration Rule
frameworks.definition: Adjust funnel friction in response to lead volume and quality: add friction when too many unqualified leads opt in; remove friction when opt-in volume is too low; if nearly no friction exists and leads are still bad, the targeting is wrong.

claims.text: Alex Hormozi asserts that local businesses are the easiest category to run paid ads for because trust is already high by default; the targeting problem is simpler and the audience already knows the service category, so lead-gen ads can be offer-driven rather than brand-building.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.topic: Platform Choice and Backup Channel Resilience
conditions: audience already aware of the service category
claims.mechanism: Geographic proximity creates inherent baseline trust that national or e-commerce advertisers must build from scratch with brand spend, so local operators can run direct offer ads without trust-building pre-frames.
bounded_by: Does not apply to national or online-only businesses selling to cold internet audiences, where trust must be built before conversion

claims.text: Alex Hormozi asserts that adding a video sales letter (VSL) to a landing page creates good friction that increases lead quality, whereas adding technical friction such as slow page load also adds friction but does not improve lead quality.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.topic: VSL as Qualification and Pre-Frame Gate
claims.mechanism: A VSL pre-frames the offer and filters uncommitted viewers before they opt in, whereas technical friction (slow load) filters randomly without self-selection on intent or fit.

claims.text: Alex Hormozi asserts that in paid advertising, adding more filters to a funnel increases cost per lead, but only good filters (e.g., VSL, application form) produce higher-quality leads; bad filters increase cost without improving quality.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Friction selects for prospects willing to invest attention or effort; quality of the filter determines whether effort-investment correlates with intent and fit.

claims.text: Alex Hormozi asserts that at Gym Launch, 80% of ad resources were spent taking existing winning ad creatives and re-skinning them into variations (black and white, sepia, reordered cuts, swapped hooks, different headlines, different ad copy), rather than producing entirely new creative concepts.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: A proven winner has already demonstrated audience resonance; variations extend the winner's reach across segments and ad fatigue thresholds without the risk of producing entirely untested creative.

numbers.axis: ad resource allocation by creative type

bounded_by: Requires at least one proven winning creative to re-skin; cannot apply at zero-winner stage

claims.text: Alex Hormozi asserts that a single winning ad creative should be re-skinned into approximately 100 variations before being retired, exhausting every combination of filter, hook, headline, subhead, font, copy angle, and structural reorder.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

numbers.axis: number of variations extracted from one winning creative

anchors.value: run until it stops working entirely

claims.text: Alex Hormozi recommends allocating ad spend and creative time in a 70-20-10 ratio: 70% on current proven winners, 20% on adjacent permutations of those winners, and 10% on experimental concepts; he applied this framework at Gym Launch and attributes it to Google's internal experimentation model.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: businesses with at least one proven winning ad creative
claims.mechanism: Concentrating spend on proven winners maximizes near-term ROAS; the 20% adjacent allocation systematically explores incremental improvements; the 10% experimental budget explores discontinuous ideas without jeopardizing stable returns.

numbers.axis: ad budget and time allocation by creative risk level

bounded_by: Requires at least one proven winner to anchor the 70% bucket; not applicable at the very start of paid media when no winner exists yet

claims.text: Alex Hormozi asserts that global retargeting across all platforms (Google Display Network, Instagram, Facebook, YouTube) for any audience that has already done a site visit almost always produces a positive ROAS because the awareness cost has already been paid and the retargeted audience has demonstrated intent.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.topic: Cross-Platform Retargeting Increases Touchpoints and Reduces CAC
conditions: any business running paid or organic traffic
claims.mechanism: Site visitors have already been filtered by initial intent; re-exposing them across platforms is low incremental cost relative to the elevated conversion probability of a warm audience.
bounded_by: Requires sufficient site traffic to build retargeting audiences; minimum viable audience size typically 1,000+ monthly visitors

claims.text: Alex Hormozi asserts that for a business with proven ROAS (citing a solar company at 7:1 ROAS and an assisted living provider at 20:1 ROAS), the correct primary lever is simply spending more money rather than optimizing the funnel further.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: capacity exists to fulfill additional demand

numbers.axis: ROAS threshold at which scaling spend becomes the primary advice

bounded_by: Does not apply when capacity is constrained; if facility has a fixed number of available spots, spend should be dialed to fill capacity at a smooth rate rather than maximized

claims.text: Alex Hormozi asserts that for a group funnel, well-executed operators convert 10% of people who opt into the free group into a paid product, achieved by getting on a call with roughly 30% of group members and closing 30-50% of those calls.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.topic: Show-Up Rate and Lead Nurture Optimization
conditions: free community-based funnel (e.g., Facebook Group, Skool)
trained setters handling DMs and engagement
claims.mechanism: A free group functions as a long-term nurture environment more engaging than an email list; sustained exposure and community trust progressively qualify members, raising conversion rates relative to cold landing-page funnels.

numbers.axis: group funnel conversion rate from opt-in to paid

bounded_by: Requires trained setters; conversion rates fall with undertrained or too-few setters

claims.text: Alex Hormozi asserts that group funnels are currently reducing cost-per-call from approximately $250 to approximately $40 across multiple industries, citing this as a broad pattern he observes repeatedly.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: businesses using a free community as the primary lead magnet
replacing cold opt-in to book-a-call funnels
claims.mechanism: The free group attracts higher-intent prospects at lower initial ad cost because the group has inherent perceived value; nurture inside the group pre-qualifies members before a call is booked, reducing friction-driven no-shows.

numbers.axis: cost per booked call by funnel type

bounded_by: Observation-based pattern across industries; exact numbers vary by market and setter quality

claims.text: Alex Hormozi asserts that proof is unique to each business while promises are not, and therefore businesses seeking differentiation in paid advertising should invest in more and better proof rather than crafting a more unique promise.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: competitive markets where multiple providers offer similar outcomes
claims.mechanism: All providers in a market converge on similar outcome promises (make more money, save time, reduce headache); proof is the only dimension genuinely unique to each business because no two businesses have identical documented results.

claims.text: Alex Hormozi asserts that proof quality in ads scales along multiple dimensions: in-person is better than virtual, live is better than recorded, a testimonial from someone who looks like the target buyer is better than one from a dissimilar person, and a result the buyer wants is better than a close-but-not-quite result.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Credibility of proof scales with the perceived difficulty of faking it; an in-person live testimonial from a look-alike buyer with the exact desired result is hardest to counterfeit and therefore most persuasive.

claims.text: Alex Hormozi asserts that for direct-to-consumer beauty brands, reaching the level of $10 million per year in revenue will require producing 10 to 50 times more ad creative output than typical brands currently produce, and that creative volume is the primary separating factor at scale.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: direct-to-consumer beauty brands competing on paid social (Meta)
claims.mechanism: Beauty is a heavily contested direct-response category; ad fatigue is rapid and creative novelty drives reach; higher creative volume means more surface area for finding winners and more variation to extend winners' lives.

numbers.axis: required creative output multiplier to reach $10M+ annual revenue in DTC beauty

bounded_by: Specific to DTC beauty paid social; multiplier may differ for other categories

claims.text: Alex Hormozi asserts that for local service businesses running paid ads, the targeting effectiveness of Meta (Facebook/Instagram) is sufficient for most avatar types, and that TikTok targeting is improving rapidly but Meta remains the safer first bet for beginners.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.topic: Platform Choice and Backup Channel Resilience
bounded_by: PPC (Google) outperforms Meta on intent-based conversion for high-ticket local services because searchers are actively looking; Meta is interruption-based

claims.text: Alex Hormozi asserts that for businesses already generating qualified traffic via PPC, Meta ads will produce lower lead quality than PPC because Meta is interruption-based marketing rather than intent-based, meaning the prospect was not actively searching when they encountered the ad.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.topic: Platform Choice and Backup Channel Resilience
conditions: high-intent service businesses (e.g., roofing) expanding from PPC to social
claims.mechanism: PPC captures in-market demand; Meta reaches audiences not actively in-market, requiring the ad to generate demand rather than capture it, producing lower baseline intent.
bounded_by: High average ticket sizes (e.g., roofing) partially compensate for lower Meta lead quality because even a lower close rate is economically viable

claims.text: Alex Hormozi asserts that compliance audit firms specializing in health-space advertising have a post-audit ad approval rate of approximately 90% or higher and typically charge $5,000-$6,000, making them a cost-effective path for health businesses whose ads are repeatedly rejected by platforms.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.topic: Platform Choice and Backup Channel Resilience
conditions: businesses in regulated verticals (health, wealth, relationships)
ads being rejected by automated platform systems
claims.mechanism: Compliance firms have established relationships and internal contacts at ad platforms; their approval of an account carries implicit endorsement that reduces automated rejection risk.

numbers.axis: compliance audit outcomes by firm quality

bounded_by: Only applies to businesses not making overtly false or prohibited health claims; firms cannot protect genuinely non-compliant content

claims.text: Alex Hormozi asserts that there is no PPC campaign bidding on a business's own branded search terms that fails to make money; owning branded PPC terms is the first and most reliable paid ad move for any business with existing organic or direct traffic.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: businesses with existing brand awareness or organic traffic
claims.mechanism: People searching for a brand's own name are already intent-qualified and aware; converting them via branded PPC costs very little and loses almost nothing to competitors.
bounded_by: Only applies when there is existing branded search volume; a brand-new business has no branded search

claims.text: Alex Hormozi asserts that bundling recurring consumables (e.g., creams or gels) as an annual pack at the point of device purchase increases average cart value because buyers are in a committed mindset at the moment of the primary purchase and are likely to reason that they will use the consumables.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: DTC hardware or device businesses with consumable accessories
bundle offered at checkout or immediately post-purchase
claims.mechanism: A customer who just bought a device has already committed to using it; in that committed mental state, adding a year's supply of accessories feels consistent with their already-made decision (reduced cognitive dissonance), producing high bundle take rates that single-item post-purchase offers do not achieve.

numbers.axis: estimated bundle take rate and ACV impact

anchors.region: ACV increase from $40 annual cream bundle on $80 device

bounded_by: Effect is strongest at point of primary purchase; post-purchase emails have significantly lower bundle conversion

claims.text: Alex Hormozi asserts that for a lead generation funnel, the correct diagnostic when there are too few qualified opt-ins despite low friction is that the targeting is wrong, not that the offer or the page is wrong.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: still receiving poor lead quality despite low friction

examples.text: Alex Hormozi describes the Kale ad from Gym Launch: Kale, who later became GM, filmed an unscripted testimonial in front of a full gym with his wife present, saying the gym was two months from closing, then fully packed within four months, fully outsourced at six months, and sold at 18 months. Hormozi made approximately 100 versions of this single ad: black and white, sepia filter, reordered back end, swapped hooks, different headlines, different subheads, changed fonts, different ad copy. He ran all variations until none performed any longer.

Alex Hormozi walks through an ad strategy for a dental recruiting business (currently advertising on job boards): target the same dentists on Meta (Facebook and Instagram) using the pain points of dentists who do not want to work weekends, do not want undesirable hours, do not want to be forced into a private equity exit requiring five years of servitude. He advises taking the client list, building a lookalike audience, and trusting that if the word 'dentist' appears in the ad copy and video, Facebook's AI will target dentists automatically.

Alex Hormozi describes a funnel strategy for a $1.2M VA business targeting home service owners: the ad explains the cost structure (e.g., a roofer paying ~$25,000 per year in labor for tasks a VA can replace at ~$6,000 per year, yielding $19,000 in savings per person). The guarantee offered is that if the client does not make five times the cost by day 90, the rest of the year of VA services is free. The creative is the founder walking through the process, paired with representative case studies of named clients (e.g., John at $10M revenue, 20 staff) and exact dollar savings.

Alex Hormozi describes a conversion path for an acupuncture business: run lead ads for a $19-$29 introductory offer. On opt-in, the thank-you page collects the card. The business calls all leads, closes them on the introductory offer to get a card on file, performs the treatment, then sells the longer care plan after the session while the patient is still in-office. The card already on file removes friction from the final close, which becomes: 'Do you want to use the card you have on file?'

Alex Hormozi describes the proof continuum using a concrete contrast: at the low end of proof quality sits an anonymous, 10-year-old, text-only testimonial with no identifying details. At the high end sits someone who walks on stage in front of the live audience, owns a CrossFit business coaching business (matching the audience avatar exactly), and says 'Alex helped me go from $3 million to $30 million' in person, not recorded. He identifies six credibility dimensions: in-person vs virtual, live vs recorded, avatar match vs no match, specific result vs generic result.

Alex Hormozi describes the vacation rental B2B funnel for an $800K business: the ad leads with the pain of having a second property sitting empty while the mortgage accrues. The free content piece contains five case studies of representative home types and avatar types, so prospects can self-identify. The bottom of the document answers the ten most common objections (trashing, security, squatters, cleaning). A free property estimate is offered at the close. If opt-ins are too unqualified, an application form is added.

Alex Hormozi describes the CrossFit / business coaching brand (Barbell Shrugged): they are brand-conscious and podcast-first with three million dollars in revenue. His advice: install pixels on every platform to start collecting retargeting data from existing podcast traffic immediately, then run PPC on branded terms, then create a high-value lead magnet (citing his own Money Models book and 11 frameworks document as examples of genuinely valuable opt-in assets), and let client testimonials drive the ads rather than founder-driven messaging.

practices.text: Install a tracking pixel for each ad platform (Meta, Google, TikTok, YouTube) on your website as soon as possible so that retargeting audiences begin building from existing traffic before you launch paid campaigns.
practices.topic: Cross-Platform Retargeting Increases Touchpoints and Reduces CAC

practices.text: For any business with existing organic or direct traffic, run a branded PPC campaign on your own brand name terms before running any other paid campaign; this is described as the highest-certainty positive-ROAS paid ad move available.
When building ad creative for a lead generation offer, lead with the target avatar's most acute pain point in the hook rather than the product features or the brand story.
Use a customer email list to build a lookalike audience on Meta before running cold traffic campaigns, especially in early-stage paid ad programs where cold targeting signals are weak.

Call all opt-ins by phone regardless of whether they booked a call, to confirm appointments and set calls for those who did not book; outbound dialing on all leads increases show rate and moves the sales cycle faster.
practices.topic: Show-Up Rate and Lead Nurture Optimization

practices.text: For a free group funnel, add an onboarding call as a bonus for every new member; use the onboarding call to diagnose the member's situation and transition to a sales conversation.
practices.topic: Show-Up Rate and Lead Nurture Optimization

practices.text: In a group funnel, have DM setters engage every person who likes, comments, or posts inside the group to book a call before organic interest cools.

For a waitlist (e.g., assisted living or capacity-constrained service), require a paid deposit to hold a spot; a free waitlist is not a real waitlist because prospects will solve their problem elsewhere before the slot opens.

For DTC hardware or device businesses, offer a bundled annual supply of consumable accessories at point of device purchase rather than as standalone post-purchase email offers; present it as a savings opportunity consistent with the buyer's already-made commitment.

When analyzing ad performance to improve ROAS, isolate the first three seconds of the top 5-10% of ads and use those hooks across all remaining creatives; you can literally splice the best opening three seconds onto 100+ existing ads to generate new variations at low cost.
